description: Cacik is a refreshing Turkish yogurt and cucumber dip, perfect for cooling down on a warm day. This delightful appetizer combines creamy strained yogurt with finely grated or diced cucumbers, fresh garlic, and a hint of mint. It is a staple on every Turkish dinner table, offering a light and flavorful accompaniment to grilled meats or as a standalone mezze.

ingredients.notes: peeled and grated or finely diced

instructions.title: Prepare the Cucumber
instructions.text: Wash and peel the cucumber. Grate it using the coarse side of a grater, or finely dice it into small pieces. If grating, gently squeeze out any excess water using a clean kitchen towel to prevent the cacik from becoming too watery.

instructions.title: Mince the Garlic
instructions.text: Peel and mince the fresh garlic cloves very finely, or crush them using a garlic press. The garlic is a key flavor component, so ensure it is well incorporated.

instructions.title: Combine Yogurt and Garlic
instructions.text: In a medium mixing bowl, add the strained yogurt. Add the minced garlic and a pinch of salt. Mix well until the garlic is evenly distributed throughout the yogurt.

instructions.title: Add Cucumber and Fresh Mint
instructions.text: Fold in the prepared cucumber and the finely chopped fresh mint into the yogurt mixture. Stir gently to combine all ingredients without overmixing.

instructions.title: Adjust Consistency and Seasoning
instructions.text: Gradually add cold water, one tablespoon at a time, while stirring, until the cacik reaches your desired consistency. Some prefer it thick, others slightly thinner. Taste and adjust salt as needed.

instructions.title: Chill Before Serving
instructions.text: Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate the cacik for at least 30 minutes. Chilling allows the flavors to meld beautifully and ensures a refreshing experience.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Before serving, transfer the chilled cacik to a serving bowl. Drizzle generously with extra virgin olive oil and sprinkle with dried mint, if using. Serve immediately with warm crusty bread, pita, or as an accompaniment to grilled dishes.

tips: Always use strained yogurt (süzme yoğurt) for an authentic, thick, and creamy texture. Regular yogurt might make the dip too watery.
For an extra layer of flavor, you can toast the dried mint lightly in a pan with a tiny bit of olive oil before sprinkling it on top.
Cacik is best served cold. Prepare it a few hours in advance and keep it refrigerated to allow the flavors to deepen and meld beautifully.
